title: Wikidata reconciliation pass (propose QID/place matches)
context: Reconciling persons and places against Wikidata (CC0) makes the corpus part of the linked-data web and enables downstream tools to join it with other datasets. However, reconciliation carries a privacy risk: incorrectly matching two different real people is both a data error and a potential privacy violation. The reconciliation pass must be precision-first — it proposes candidate matches with confidence scores but never merges automatically. All proposed matches go to a human review worklist before any merge is applied. Place matching similarly proposes Wikidata QIDs for PlaceReference nodes but does not auto-apply.
objective: Run a Wikidata reconciliation pass over the M1 corpus persons and places, generating a candidate-match worklist with blocking keys, confidence scores, and match evidence for each proposed pairing, ready for human review in the recon-002 task.
acceptanceCriteria: Reconciliation uses an explicit blocking-key strategy (e.g., normalized surname + birth-decade + birthplace region for persons; normalized place name + administrative hierarchy for places).
Matcher tuned for precision over recall: only high-confidence candidates are surfaced; low-confidence candidates are flagged as 'uncertain' rather than promoted.
Output is a structured candidate-match worklist (JSON or YAML) with: corpus entity ID, proposed Wikidata QID, confidence score, blocking keys matched, and supporting evidence snippet.
No automatic merges applied; all candidates go to the human review worklist.
Wikidata source data used is CC0 (Wikidata labels/statements); the derived reconciliation dataset is labeled CC0-1.0.
Candidate-match worklist committed to reconciliation/candidates/ via PR with a summary of total candidates, confidence distribution, and any obvious false-positive patterns observed.
output: reconciliation/candidates/<batch-id>-wikidata-candidates.json — structured candidate-match worklist for human review, committed via PR.
